# clean_exif_data

[← Command index](README.md)

Strip all EXIF and other embedded metadata from image files.

## Synopsis

```
clean_exif_data [options]
```

## Description

Runs ExifTool with `-All=` over the input, removing every writable metadata tag
(camera, GPS location, timestamps, thumbnails and so on). A directory is processed
recursively. Files are rewritten in place with `-overwrite_original`, so no backup
copies are left behind.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Image file, or directory to process recursively; it must exist. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Strip metadata from one photo

```bash
clean_exif_data -i ~/Pictures/photo.jpg
```

### Strip metadata from every file in a directory tree

```bash
clean_exif_data -i ~/Pictures/ToShare
```

### Dry run, leaving every file untouched

```bash
clean_exif_data -i ~/Pictures/ToShare -p -v
```

## Notes

- The change cannot be undone; copy anything whose metadata you want to keep first.
- ExifTool must be installed with `setup_tools -k ExifTool`.
